title: Ambiguous metric notation triage log
content:
Notes / problem statement:

We keep seeing noisy metric shorthand in incoming text fields that breaks downstream parsers and makes labeling inconsistent. Examples: "5k", "5 k", "5K+", "5-6k", "1e3", "~3k/mo", "5k users", "5k (est)", "5k+/month", "£5k", "5k GBP", "5k/yr", "5k–June". Also weird items like "ms" vs "m s", "s" that may be seconds or string suffixes.

This doc is my scratchpad for a minimal, pragmatic adjudication and normalization protocol so labelers and adjudicators have a quick set of rules and examples. High-level goals:
- Keep gold labels useful for product analytics and model training (canonical numeric + unit where feasible)
- Minimize adjudicator cognitive load (simple heuristics to catch ~95% patterns)
- Tolerate ambiguous cases with clear fallback tags so downstream systems can decide.

Quick terminology / desired output shape:
- canonical_value: normalized numeric string in base units (no commas, explicit multiplier applied). e.g. "5000"
- canonical_unit: short standardized unit token, e.g. "users", "USD", "ms", "s", "per_month"
- label_tags: list of short tags for ambiguity e.g. AMBIG_UNIT, ESTIMATED, RANGE, RAW_TEXT_REQUIRED

Decision tree (labeler flow) - try to make this a quick checklist:
1) Can we parse an explicit currency symbol or currency code? (e.g., $/£/EUR/GBP) --> prefer currency unit (USD/GBP/EUR). Strip symbol, parse multiplier (k/m) and return canonical_value and canonical_unit=USD/GBP/etc.
2) Is it a clear multiplier suffix (k, K, M, m, B, b) possibly with punctuation (5k, 5 k, 5K+)? If so, expand: k -> *1000, M -> *1e6. If ambiguous lower-case m appears with other context indicating month or meter, prefer context (look for /mo, /yr, month) else treat as million if adjacent to number and not separated by space? Put AMBIG_MULTIPLIER tag if we had to guess.
3) Does the string contain a range (e.g., 5-6k, 5k to 6k, ~5k-6k)? If yes, canonical_value = lower_bound after expansion (use lower to be conservative), add RANGE tag and store raw_text.
4) Suffixes "/mo", "per mo", "/m", "/month": normalize to canonical_unit per_month. Similarly "/yr", "/year" -> per_year.
5) Scientific notation (1e3, 2E4) -> parse as numeric. Keep original if weird capitalization but normalize.
6) Percent signs: keep as percent (canonical_unit = percent) and canonical_value = numeric without % sign.
7) Ambiguous short tokens that might be textual ("ms" could be "milliseconds" or initials) -> if adjacent to a numeric and context suggests timing (latency, delay, response) then ms->milliseconds; otherwise tag AMBIG_UNIT and leave raw_text.
8) If the token sits inside a product name (eg. "Plan 5k", "Series 5K") and does not appear to be a measured metric, tag RAW_TEXT_REQUIRED and annotate as LABEL_TEXT.
9) If extractor can't confidently map to a unit/number, capture raw_text and tag RAW_UNPARSED with short rationale.

Heuristics / regex suggestions (implementer notes):
- common multiplier regex: (?i)\b([0-9]{1,3}(?:[.,][0-9]{3})*|[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?)\s*([kmbKMBD]?)\b  // map suffixes k->1e3 M->1e6 B/D? review
- scientific: (?i)\b([0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?)[eE]([+-]?[0-9]+)\b
- range: ([0-9.,]+\s*[kKmMbB]?)[ \ -–to]+([0-9.,]+\s*[kKmMbB]?)\b  -> pick lower after normalize
- per unit: /\s*(mo|month|yr|year|yr\.|y) or (per\s+mo|per\s+month)
- currency symbol: ^[\$£€¥]\s*\d or trailing currency codes: (USD|GBP|EUR|JPY|CAD)\b

Canonicalizer examples (examples we can add to dataset):
- "5k" -> canonical_value=5000, canonical_unit=none (or users if context reveals), tags=[MULTIPLIER_EXPANDED]
- "5k users" -> canonical_value=5000, canonical_unit=users, tags=[MULTIPLIER_EXPANDED]
- "~5k+/mo" -> canonical_value=5000, canonical_unit=per_month, tags=[ESTIMATED, MULTIPLIER_EXPANDED, RANGE?] (note: prefer ESTIMATED)
- "1e3" -> canonical_value=1000, canonical_unit=none, tags=[SCIENTIFIC_NOTATION]
- "£5k" -> canonical_value=5000, canonical_unit=GBP, tags=[CURRENCY_SYMBOL]
- "5k-6k" -> canonical_value=5000, canonical_unit=none, tags=[RANGE]
- "5k+" -> canonical_value=5000, canonical_unit=none, tags=[GREATER_THAN, MULTIPLIER_EXPANDED]
- "5k/month" -> canonical_value=5000, canonical_unit=per_month, tags=[PERIODIC]
- "V3" or "5K Series" -> RAW_TEXT_REQUIRED, tags=[CONTAINS_PRODUCT_CODE]

Adjudication quick rules (for the human reviewer):
- If multiplier choice is ambiguous (m vs M), prefer million (M) for uppercase M, prefer thousand for lowercase k; if "m" ambiguous and context indicates time ("m" after number and words like "mo" absent) -> tag AMBIG_MULTIPLIER and ask for sample-based correction.
- Currency without code: map $ -> USD by default unless country context suggests otherwise; tag ASSUMED_USD if inferred.
- If text looks like a marketing string (numbers adjacent to campaign names), mark as TEXT_NOT_METRIC.

Sampling queries for QA (to build adjudication batch):
- regex samples: "\b[0-9]+\s*[kKmMbB]\b" (get 10k hits)
- ranges: "\b[0-9]+\s*[-–to]\s*[0-9]+\s*[kKmMbB]?\b"
- currency with symbol but no code: "\b[\$£€]\s*[0-9]+[kKmM]?\b"
- scientific notation: "\b[0-9]+e[+-]?[0-9]+\b"

Open questions / tradeoffs (to resolve in design doc):
- How to treat ambiguous single-letter suffixes (m) at scale without manual review budget? Do we default to million or default to treat as month? Both choices bias downstream metrics differently.
- Do we keep canonical_unit empty when unit isn't explicitly present, or infer "users" or "count" when text appears like user counts? Current thinking: keep empty + tag INFERRED_COUNT if we infer.
- Should we return numeric as integer string only or allow float strings (e.g. 2.5k -> 2500)? Prefer integer when multiplier expansion yields integer; allow decimals where appropriate and preserve minimal precision.

QA checklist for batch sampling before merging into gold set:
- Random sample of 500 expanded multiplier cases: check expansion accuracy >= 98%
- 200 currency symbol cases: check currency mapping correctness >= 99% or tag ASSUMED_{CURRENCY}
- 300 ranges: ensure lower-bound policy applied consistently
- 100 ambiguous unit cases (ms ambiguity etc): verify AMBIG_UNIT tag applied appropriately

Labeler quick cheat-sheet (one line each):
- See currency symbol? Map symbol to currency, expand multiplier, tag ASSUMED if inferred.
- Range? Use lower bound, tag RANGE.
- "+" or "approx"? Tag ESTIMATED.
- Scientific? Expand. 
- If product name or code suspected -> RAW_TEXT_REQUIRED.

To-do / action items:
- Create a small test harness that runs the regexes on a 1M-row sample and surfaces top 200 ambiguous tokens for manual review (Diego).
- Add a short labeling UI note (Maya) that surfaces example of what to do when encountering "m" vs "M" ambiguity.
- Draft final rule for currency defaults in the design doc (me).

Random examples pulled during quick grep (real-ish) - annotate mentally:
- "500k users" -> parse ok
- "5k USD/mo" -> ok
- "5k GBP" -> ok
- "Plan 5K" -> prob product code not metric
- "avg latency ~5 ms" -> treat as ms unless context contradicts
- "1e3 signups" -> expand to 1000 signups
- "5k+ installs" -> canonical=5000 tag GREATER_THAN

Notes to future self: keep heuristics conservative and explicit. It's better to return an explicit tag signaling inference than silently normalize into a possibly wrong unit. Labelers should get fast binary choices; adjudicators should be used only for the tail.

End of scratchpad for now. Will convert to a formal quick-reference card once we codify the default decisions on "m" and default currency mapping.

-- Ava
